newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan oil expert sees Dubai price at $17-$19/bbl.
newsitem.headline: Japan oil expert sees Dubai price at $17-$19/bbl.

text.p: The price of Dubai crude this year is likely to average between $17-$19 per barrel, or slightly below its 1996 average, barring unexpected global developments, a Japanese oil expert said on Thursday.

"I think (prices) will be a little weaker than last year... Dubai's price will (probably average) about $17 to $19 (this year)," Makoto Satani, general manager of Nippon Oil Co Ltd's petroleum supply department, told reporters.
Last year Dubai traded at an average of $18.60, he said.
The price of Dubai so far this year has averaged roughly a little over $18.
The forecast is based on the supply/demand balance of global crude oil, he said.
He offered figures from the International Energy Agency (IEA), which showed that in 1996 crude oil supplies amounted to 72 million barrels per day (bpd) compared with demand of 71.9 million bpd.
The IEA's forecast for 1997 shows crude oil supplies at 75.2 million bpd compared with demand of 73.7 million bpd.

On the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries' (OPEC) ministerial meeting, due to be held in Vienna from June 25, he said news related to the meeting so far indicated that OPEC was likely to decide to maintain its current production quota of 25.03 million bpd.
Satani said he believed OPEC members would like to see Dubai traded at a level over $16 for the rest of the year.
"In terms of crude oil prices I think they (OPEC) would like to see Dubai at a level over $16 (per barrel), although they do not say this in so many words, he said.
Satani noted that many OPEC nations' finances were heavily dependant on crude oil revenues and that Dubai crude would have to trade at a level over $16 to support their current finances.
